category_title: Older adolescents with severe CHARGE syndrome and challenging behaviors
minimal_context: David is sitting in the classroom working on a table-top object sorting activity.
dialogue:
TUTOR: David, it is time for your table-top activities. Here are the objects for sorting.

STUDENT: (David sits at the table but does not sort the objects, engaging in visual self-stimulatory behavior and teeth grinding instead.)

TUTOR: Look at the objects on the table. Put them in the right places.

STUDENT: (David pushes the sorting objects away, continuing to grind his teeth, and begins jumping up from his chair.)

TUTOR: Sit back down. You need to finish sorting these objects.

STUDENT: (David begins kicking and scratching to escape the activity.)

options.A: Provide David with a greater variety of functional and interesting table-top activities, ensuring his educational program is comprehensive and incorporates daily living skills.
options.B: Provide David with enthusiastic verbal praise and encouragement during the table-top activities, expressing pride in his work and verbally prompting him to keep going.
options.C: Provide David with opportunities to compromise and negotiate during the table-top activities, sharing decisions and power with him instead of imposing strict adult control.
options.D: Provide David with three repetitions of the instructions during the table-top activities, attempting to meet his needs through repeated delivery of the task demands.
